en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Section on the Puzzling Questions, Chapter on the Knowledge of Omniscience.
10. The Question on the Omniscience of the Buddha “Venerable Nāgasena, you say:
‘The Tathāgata is omniscient.’”
And yet you say:
"When the Tathāgata had dismissed the Saṅgha of bhikkhus headed by Sāriputta and Moggallāna,
the Sakyans of Cātumā and Brahmā Sahampati, having presented the similes of the seed and the young calf, gained the favor of the Blessed One."
"‘They asked for forgiveness and made amends.
Now, venerable Nāgasena, were those similes unknown to the Tathāgata, by means of which the Tathāgata was appeased, calmed, and brought to a state of reconciliation?

If, venerable Nāgasena, those similes were unknown to the Tathāgata, then the Buddha is not omniscient. If they were known, then he sent them away abruptly, having overpowered them and requiring further investigation; in that case, cruelty on his part would be possible."
“This too is a dilemma with two sides that has come to you;
it must be resolved by you. “The Tathāgata, Great King, is omniscient. By means of those similes, the Blessed One was pleased, gratified, calmed, and brought to a state of inner peace.

The Tathāgata, Great King, is the Lord of Dhamma. It was through those very similes proclaimed by the Tathāgata that they pleased, satisfied, and gladdened him. And the Tathāgata, being pleased with them, gave his approval, saying, ‘Excellent!’”
"Just as, Great King, a woman wins over, satisfies, and pleases her husband with wealth that belongs solely to her husband,
and the husband approves of this, saying, 'Excellent!'; even so, Great King, the Cātumeyyakas and the Sakyans, together with Brahmā Sahampati, won over, satisfied,
and pleased the Tathāgata with similes proclaimed by the Tathāgata himself, and the Tathāgata, being pleased with them, approved, saying, 'Excellent!'"
Or again, Great King, just as a goldsmith, by adorning the king’s head with a golden crest belonging to the king himself, gratifies, satisfies, and pleases the king;
and the king, being pleased with him, expresses his approval saying "Excellent!
and bestows upon him whatever he desires.
In the same way, Great King, the Cātumeyyakas and the Sakyans pleased, satisfied, and gladdened the Tathāgata with similes proclaimed by the Tathāgata himself;
and the Tathāgata, being pleased with them, gave his approval, saying, “Excellent!
Or again, Great King, it is like a co-resident disciple who, having received alms-food brought by his preceptor, [presents it] to the preceptor.
Just as one who presents [a gift] pleases, satisfies, and gladdens the preceptor, and the preceptor, being pleased,
expresses his approval saying "Excellent!", even so, Great King, both the Cātumeyyakas and the Sakyans,
through similes proclaimed by the Tathāgata himself, pleased, satisfied, and gladdened the Tathāgata, and the Tathāgata, being pleased with them, expressed his approval saying "Excellent!"
Having expressed his approval, he taught the Dhamma for the sake of liberation from all suffering.
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena! It is so; I accept it as such.
This is the tenth dilemma: on the omniscience of the Buddha.
The fourth chapter, on the Knowledge of Omniscience.
In this chapter there are ten questions.
